newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng scores third straight record close.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng scores third straight record close.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index capped a record-breaking week with its third consecutive all-time closing high on Friday, with gains in the banking sector offsetting profit-taking among property counters.
The index rose 25.72 points, or 0.19 percent, to close at 13,856.40, after reaching a session high of 13,977.54. Turnover was HK$13.51 billion compared with Thursday's HK$16.23 billion.
"In general market sentiment is still quite bullish," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
"I think entering 1997 we sense that more foreigners want to buy shares in Hong Kong," he said.
Buying was concentrated on the banking sector this session, with investors anticipating strong upcoming earnings reports.
HSBC Holdings rose HK$2.00 to HK$183.00 after reaching an all-time high of HK$184.50.
Hang Seng Bank advanced HK$1.00 to HK$95.50 and Bank of East Asia added HK$0.30 to HK$37.20.
"In general 1996 was still a very good year for banks despite growing competition in the second half of the year. The buoyant property market also helped their earnings," said Tsang.
But some property counters weakened on Friday, succumbing to profit-taking after a strong week.
Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$1.50 to HK$93.75 and Sino Land slipped HK$0.10 to HK$9.30.

"Cumulative gains this week are quite high so it is time to take a break," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research. The Hang Seng index rose 664.90 points, or 5.04 percent, this week.

Chia said after some consolidation, the blue-chip index was likely to move higher, with overseas interest expected to boost prices. "Even though the Hang Seng index has moved up quite sharply since 1996, the market rating is still relatively low compared with other regional markets," he said.

Confidence that Hong Kong's transition to Chinese rule should go smoothly, along with optimism about economic growth, may prompt investors to "reconsider whether the Hong Kong market deserves to trade at a discount to regional markets," Chia said.
"We have a very bullish property market," added Tsang. "A buoyant property market makes everyone happy."
Wah Lee Holdings made its trading debut on Friday and closed at HK$1.46 compared versus its issue price of HK$1.00 per share.
China Overseas, which issued 394.38 million shares at HK$3.875 per share, held steady at HK$4.05.
